investigation.root_cause: AuthTokenServerService.alterHttpRequest() (logger.service.ts:8-16) unconditionally clones every ngx-logger remote log HTTP request and adds Authorization: Bearer <token> header. The token is read directly from sessionStorage['gx_token'] (logger.service.ts:19) — bypassing the StorageService abstraction. If serverLoggingUrl is configured in the Angular environment, every ERROR-level log event generates an HTTP request to the remote log endpoint carrying the full Bearer token. This expands the credential attack surface beyond ApplinX REST API to a second, potentially less-secured log infrastructure endpoint.
investigation.attack_scenario:
Log Infrastructure Compromise: Attacker compromises the ngx-logger remote endpoint (e.g., /logger path at the ApplinX server or a separate log aggregation service). The attacker can extract Bearer tokens from all incoming log requests. Each error log during a session includes the user's current token, enabling full session replay.

HTTP Log Endpoint: If serverLoggingUrl uses HTTP (not HTTPS), tokens are transmitted in cleartext and susceptible to network-level interception.

Log File Exposure: Log entries shipped to the remote endpoint may contain raw error messages from ApplinX server (VULN-011) including stack traces, screen names, and session details — compound information disclosure.

Direct sessionStorage Read: logger.service.ts:19 bypasses StorageService, meaning StorageService refactoring (e.g., moving to httpOnly cookie) would not automatically fix this logger — it must be updated independently.
prerequisites: serverLoggingUrl must be configured in Angular environment (log shipping must be active)
An ERROR-level log event must occur during the session (error, disconnect, failed API call)
Attacker must intercept HTTP traffic or compromise the log endpoint

privilege_boundary.start_privilege: Network attacker or log infrastructure access
privilege_boundary.achieved_privilege: Bearer token extracted from log request headers — full ApplinX session hijack possible

impact.description: If remote logging is active, the Bearer token is transmitted with every log request. Interception or log infrastructure compromise yields a valid session token. Combined with VULN-011 (raw server error messages in logs), the remote log endpoint receives both the authentication credential AND sensitive server internals. This is a conditional vulnerability — severity depends entirely on whether serverLoggingUrl is configured in production.

transformations: httpRequest.clone({ setHeaders: { Authorization: token } }) — injected into every remote log request
sinks: Remote log HTTP endpoint (serverLoggingUrl) — receives Bearer token in Authorization header with every log request

direct.impact: Unconditional Bearer token injection into log requests
Direct sessionStorage access bypassing StorageService abstraction

indirect.impact: Second credential surface — distinct from ApplinX REST API
Raw server error messages also shipped to log endpoint — compound information disclosure

remediation_guidance.recommended_fix: Remove the Authorization header from log requests entirely — log endpoints do not require user session tokens for authentication. If log endpoint authentication is needed, use a dedicated log-specific API key (not the user's session Bearer token). Update getAuthToken() to use StorageService rather than direct sessionStorage access.
defense_in_depth: Remove Bearer token from log request Authorization header
Use a separate log-specific authentication credential if log endpoint requires auth
Update logger.service.ts to use StorageService.getAuthToken() instead of direct sessionStorage read
Sanitize log message content to remove sensitive data before shipping

external: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information
OWASP A09:2021 — Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
